description:
Relais Castello di Razzano is a historic residence with more than 200 years of history, set in an enclosed courtyard surrounded by Italian countryside. The property was acquired by the Olearo family in 1968 from the Caligaris family, and the old coaching inn that forms part of the complex was built centuries ago at the heart of the estate.

Today the castle operates as a charming relais within a 100-hectare estate dedicated to wine and olive oil production, in the heart of the Monferrato, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Guests are welcomed directly by the Olearo family, who personally share their connection to the castle and the territory.

The Olearo family's more than five decades of ownership since 1968, following the earlier Caligaris tenure, gives Razzano a genuinely personal, family-run character distinct from corporately managed resort properties elsewhere in this collection.

The estate's coaching inn origins, built centuries before the current residence, point to Razzano's historical role along a regional travel route, a function distinct from the purely defensive or agricultural origins of many other Piedmontese estates.

The 100-hectare scale of the wine and olive estate places Razzano among the more substantial working agricultural properties in this collection, situated within a landscape recognized by UNESCO specifically for the relationship between its communities and their vine-growing territory.

The surrounding Monferrato UNESCO wine route and nearby towns of Casale Monferrato and Asti give guests staying at Razzano direct access to one of Piedmont's most internationally recognized wine landscapes.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Razzano Castle within the historic building?
faqs.answer: Yes — the 12-13 rooms and suites, ranging from 30 to 120 square meters, are all within the historic building of the former residence and coaching inn, with no separate annex identified.

faqs.question: Who runs Razzano Castle?
faqs.answer: The Olearo family, who have owned the property since 1968 and personally welcome guests, sharing their own connection to the castle and the surrounding land.

faqs.question: How large is the Razzano estate?
faqs.answer: 100 hectares, dedicated to wine and olive oil production, within the Monferrato UNESCO World Heritage landscape.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** Under 1 hour from Milan, Turin and Genoa by car; Turin's Caselle Airport (TRN) is about 1 hour away.

**Rooms & rates:** 12-13 rooms and suites (30 to 120 square meters) within the historic building of the former residence/coaching inn, with panoramic views of the vineyard hills. From €99/night.

**On-site:** Own winery and small museum, 100-hectare estate of vineyards and olive groves.

**Good to know:** The Olearo family's personal, hands-on hospitality is one of the property's defining features — this is not an anonymously managed hotel, but a family home open to guests.

**Combine with:** Alfiano Natta, the Monferrato UNESCO wine route, Casale Monferrato, Asti.
